title: Flat scalar restriction transports the strict-diagram adjunction mate
statement:
Let $\mathscr X,\mathscr Y,\mathscr X',\mathscr Y'$ be topoi on small sites with a specified commutative square having edges $f:\mathscr X\to\mathscr Y$, $f':\mathscr X'\to\mathscr Y'$, $g:\mathscr Y'\to\mathscr Y$, $g':\mathscr X'\to\mathscr X$. At each corner $T$ let $a_T:R_T\to S_T$ be a map of commutative ring sheaves with $S_T$ flat over $R_T$. For every edge $u:U\to V$ specify isomorphisms $u^{-1}R_V\cong R_U$ and $u^{-1}S_V\cong S_U$ commuting with $a_T$, and assume the two composite coefficient identifications along the square agree for each coefficient system [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Use $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op}$ strict diagrams, their small ringed diagram sites [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], and unbounded derived module categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $r_T$ for termwise restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $L_u^R\dashv F_u^R$ and $L_u^S\dashv F_u^S$ denote derived termwise module inverse/direct image, with the specified termwise adjunction derived as in [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general]. Use the canonical pullback composition maps from the specified geometric square and coefficient identifications. Let $E^R:L_g^RF_f^R\to F_{f'}^RL_{g'}^R$ and $E^S:L_g^SF_f^S\to F_{f'}^SL_{g'}^S$ be their adjunction mates [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. For every edge let $p_u:r_UL_u^S\cong L_u^Rr_V$ and $d_u:r_VF_u^S\cong F_u^Rr_U$ be exactly the normalized flat restriction comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-restriction].

The $p_u$ identify the two canonical pullback composition squares, including their coefficient actions. For an arbitrary $Z\in D(\operatorname{Fun}(J,\operatorname{Mod}(S_X)))$, define
$$b_Z=(L_g^Rd_{f,Z})p_{g,F_f^SZ},\qquad d_Z=(F_{f'}^Rp_{g',Z})d_{f',L_{g'}^SZ}.$$
Then $b_Z:r_{Y'}L_g^SF_f^SZ\cong L_g^RF_f^Rr_XZ$ and $d_Z:r_{Y'}F_{f'}^SL_{g'}^SZ\cong F_{f'}^RL_{g'}^Rr_XZ$ satisfy
$$d_Z\,r_{Y'}(E_Z^S)=E^R_{r_XZ}b_Z.$$
More explicitly the transpose of $d_Zr_{Y'}(E_Z^S)b_Z^{-1}$ under $L_{f'}^R\dashv F_{f'}^R$ is $L_{g'}^R(\varepsilon^R_{f,r_XZ})\theta^R_{F_f^Rr_XZ}$, where $\theta^R:L_{f'}^RL_g^R\cong L_{g'}^RL_f^R$ is that canonical pullback square. All assertions are natural in the actual derived strict tower $Z$; no reduction-tower, completeness or cartesianness assumption is required.

proof.text: At each diagram component apply the faithful underlying set-sheaf functor. Compose with the two invertible R module-underlying comparisons. The four ordinary normalization equations, naturality of the module-underlying comparisons and equality transport along sameInverse reduce both paths to the common geometric square; sameGeometry identifies its two presentations. This proves the ordinary module square, including its actions. Apply this equation in each cochain degree. Compose the four given localization factors using functor associators and whiskering. Naturality and cancellation of the invertible factors transport the ordinary square to objects in the image of DerivedCategory.Q. Localization.natTrans_ext detects equality of the two derived natural transformations. Evaluating that equality gives the first conjunct (C).

proof.text:
Fix $Z$ and put $A=F_f^SZ$. Apply (A) for $u=f$ to $t=\varepsilon^S_{f,Z}:L_f^SA\to Z$, whose adjunct is $1_A$. The adjunct of $r_X(\varepsilon^S_{f,Z})p_{f,A}^{-1}$ is therefore $d_{f,Z}$. By the counit formula for the inverse adjunction bijection this says
$$r_X(\varepsilon^S_{f,Z})p_{f,A}^{-1}=\varepsilon^R_{f,r_XZ}\,L_f^R(d_{f,Z}).$$
Precomposing with $L_f^R(d_{f,Z}^{-1})$ gives the normalized counit equation
$$r_X(\varepsilon^S_{f,Z})p_{f,A}^{-1}L_f^R(d_{f,Z}^{-1})=\varepsilon^R_{f,r_XZ}.\tag{K}$$

proof.text:
By [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], $E^S_Z$ is the adjunct of
$$e^S_Z=L_{g'}^S(\varepsilon^S_{f,Z})\theta^S_A:L_{f'}^SL_g^SA\longrightarrow L_{g'}^SZ.$$
Set $h_Z=d_Zr_{Y'}(E^S_Z)b_Z^{-1}$. Formula (A) for $f'$ says that $d_{f',L_{g'}^SZ}r_{Y'}(E^S_Z)$ is the adjunct of $r_{X'}(e^S_Z)p_{f',L_g^SA}^{-1}$. Postcomposition with $F_{f'}^R(p_{g',Z})$ and precomposition with $b_Z^{-1}$ therefore show that the transpose of $h_Z$ is
$$t_Z=p_{g',Z}\,r_{X'}(e^S_Z)\,p_{f',L_g^SA}^{-1}L_{f'}^R(b_Z^{-1}).\tag{T}$$
The pre/postcomposition rule here follows directly by expanding transpose as counit followed by $L_{f'}^R$ of the morphism and using counit naturality.

proof.text:
Expand $e^S_Z$ in (T). Naturality of $p_{g'}$ at $\varepsilon^S_{f,Z}$ rewrites its first two factors as
$$p_{g',Z}\,r_{X'}(L_{g'}^S\varepsilon^S_{f,Z})=L_{g'}^R(r_X\varepsilon^S_{f,Z})p_{g',L_f^SA}.$$
Equation (C) at $A$, cancelling $L_{g'}^Rp_{f,A}$, now gives
$$t_Z=L_{g'}^R(r_X\varepsilon^S_{f,Z})\,(L_{g'}^Rp_{f,A})^{-1}\theta^R_{r_YA}\,L_{f'}^R(p_{g,A}b_Z^{-1}).$$
The definition $b_Z=(L_g^Rd_{f,Z})p_{g,A}$ yields $p_{g,A}b_Z^{-1}=L_g^R(d_{f,Z}^{-1})$. Thus
$$t_Z=L_{g'}^R(r_X\varepsilon^S_{f,Z}\,p_{f,A}^{-1})\theta^R_{r_YA}\,L_{f'}^RL_g^R(d_{f,Z}^{-1}).\tag{T'}$$
Every replacement is naturality or cancellation of a specified isomorphism.

proof.text:
Use naturality of $\theta^R$ at $d_{f,Z}^{-1}:F_f^Rr_XZ\to r_YA$ in (T'). It moves the last factor across $\theta^R$, giving
$$t_Z=L_{g'}^R\bigl(r_X\varepsilon^S_{f,Z}\,p_{f,A}^{-1}L_f^R(d_{f,Z}^{-1})\bigr)\theta^R_{F_f^Rr_XZ}.$$
Substitute (K). The result is
$$t_Z=L_{g'}^R(\varepsilon^R_{f,r_XZ})\theta^R_{F_f^Rr_XZ},$$
which is precisely the transpose of $E^R_{r_XZ}$ by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection gives $h_Z=E^R_{r_XZ}$; compose on the right with $b_Z$ to obtain $d_Zr_{Y'}(E^S_Z)=E^R_{r_XZ}b_Z$. This also proves the asserted explicit transpose formula.
